about.title: Milpitas Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Milpitas is a city of roughly 77,600 people, and much of daily life here happens on property someone else controls: stores and restaurants clustered near the I-880, I-680 and Rt 237 corridors, apartment complexes, office parks, parking structures, and public sidewalks. When one of those places has a hazard that should have been fixed or flagged, and you get hurt because of it, California premises liability law may give you a path to recover your losses. The core question is almost always notice. Did the owner or operator know about the spill, the loose tile, the missing handrail, or should they have known with reasonable inspection? Answering that takes evidence, and evidence disappears quickly. Floors get mopped, incident reports get filed away, and surveillance footage is often overwritten within days. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects injured Milpitas residents with an independent attorney who can send a preservation letter, gather records, and evaluate your claim on contingency. If your fall happened on city, county, or state property, note that the deadline to act is far shorter than the usual two years.

whyChoose.title: Why Milpitas Residents Use LawProactive After a Fall

items.title: Notice is the whole case, and evidence fades fast
items.desc: California requires you to show the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney can act quickly to demand that surveillance video, cleaning logs, and inspection records be preserved before they are gone.

items.title: Deadlines differ depending on who owns the property
items.desc: Most Milpitas premises claims carry a two-year filing window, but a fall on public property, such as a city sidewalk or a county building, involves a much shorter claim deadline. Getting connected early keeps your options open.

items.title: Partial fault does not end your claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if an insurer argues you were distracted or wearing the wrong shoes, your recovery is reduced by your share of fault rather than eliminated. Your attorney will push back on inflated blame.

items.question: I fell in a store parking lot near Rt 237 in Milpitas. Who is responsible, the store or the property owner?
items.answer: It depends on who controlled and maintained the area where you fell, and often more than one party shares that duty. Leases frequently split responsibility between a tenant business and a landlord or property management company. An attorney can pull the relevant agreements and identify every party that owed you a safe premises.

items.question: What should I do right after a slip and fall in Milpitas?
items.answer: Get medical care first, even if you think you can walk it off, because fall injuries often worsen over the following days. Photograph the hazard, the lighting, and any warning signs (or their absence) before anything is cleaned up, and ask for an incident report. Collect names of witnesses and note whether cameras were pointed at the spot, since footage is commonly erased within a short window.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is free to use and is not itself a law firm. The independent attorneys in our network handle premises liability cases on contingency, meaning no fee is owed unless there is a recovery in your case. You are never required to hire the attorney you are matched with.
